1.note: Prov 13:17 "a faithful envoy (צִיר אֱמוּנִים) is healing". Here צִיר is read as "pang", so the healing envoy becomes a lasting pain.

2.note: Uncertain. אֱמוּנֵי may mean "steadfast, lasting" or "those reared on" (compare Lam 4:5 הָאֱמֻנִים עֲלֵי תוֹלָע): "a couch of those reared on sores". מָזוֹר means both "wound" and "cure".

3.note: תְּלִי is Esau's quiver in Gen 27:3. Here it seems to stand for the physician's bag of drugs.

4.note: A play on מָזוֹר, which means both "cure" and "wound" (Jer 30:13, Hos 5:13): "a mazor for every mazor".

5.note: A play on קְרָבִים (inward parts) and קְרָבוֹת (battles).

6.note: A play on תַּעֲלֶה (you will bring up) and תְּעָלָה (healing, new flesh, Jer 30:13). Line 112 plays in the same way on מָזוֹר לִמְזוֹרֶךָ, "a cure for your wound".

7.note: כְּפוֹר is "frost" (Ps 147:16), the white hands of the beloved. It is also a "bowl" (Ezra 1:10), so "the bowl of the hands" is possible.

8.note: A play on פְּרִי (fruit) and פְּרִידָה (parting).

9.note: A play on the hero's name חֶבֶר (Ḥever) and חָבֵר (companion).
